title: One-step invertible action policy with compact skill coordinates
hypothesis: A shared invertible action map plus compact per-skill adapter coordinates retains one-step action quality with lower complete bytes than independent skill policies, without adding iterative inference calls.

model.adapter: two shared Givens plane rotations with skill-specific angles

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after exact native Givens alias or frozen byte/quality gate miss.

controls: independent full invertible policy matrix per skill
Mirror skill-angle code over shared invertible base
native Givens adapter with ordinary per-skill angles
four-evaluation straight-line flow sampler as iterative-compute reference
metrics: task success fraction at fixed action tolerance
pass_gate: Test action nRMSE <=0.02, success >=0.95, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent, one-step execution, and strict improvement over native Givens control.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim for native Givens alias, quality/success miss, savings below 25%, or extra one-step latency/compute without frontier gain.

compute.active_MACs: dense shared policy plus two Givens rotations; iterative reference performs four flow evaluations
compute.wall_time: small CPU synthetic action batch; no robot latency claim

boundaries: Synthetic linear action targets only; no robot simulator, manipulation dataset, or hardware evaluation.
Skill IDs are known and charged; no skill inference claim.
The flow reference integrates a known straight-line conditional vector field; it is not a trained diffusion policy.
Native Givens is the cheapest ordinary parameter control and is expected to be functionally equivalent.
